finding.claim: Authorization bypass in the ban endpoint. require_admin() denies access by calling abort(403), which raises an HTTPException. The bare `except Exception` in ban() catches it and only logs a warning, so execution continues to do_ban(uid). Any authenticated non-admin user can ban any user.
finding.source: Any authenticated non-admin user sending POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban, where uid is attacker-chosen.

trace.note: require_admin(g.user) is called inside a try block.
A non-admin hits abort(403), which raises werkzeug HTTPException (subclass of Exception).
The failure is only logged. There is no re-raise or return.
do_ban(uid) executes unconditionally and the endpoint returns ok=True.

finding.guards_checked: The require_admin check is correct in itself but its result is discarded. unban() at line 26 calls it outside a try block, so that endpoint is properly guarded. No other decorators, before_request hooks or middleware exist in the file. If g.user is None or unset, the handler would also fail on g.user.get at line 19, but that is a secondary issue. The log line also writes the user-supplied name, which is minor log-injection exposure.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin() (admin.py:9-11) aborts with 403 on failure, but the call at admin.py:17 sits inside try/except Exception (16-19), which swallows the HTTPException. There is no re-raise or return, so nothing blocks do_ban at line 20. No decorators, before_request hooks or middleware exist.
verdict.reason: At admin.py:17-20 the abort(403) raised by require_admin (abort is at line 11; the trace cites line 10, the adjacent `if`) is caught by `except Exception` and only logged, so do_ban(uid) runs for any non-admin user, whereas unban() at admin.py:26 is unguarded by try and is safe.

verdict_facts.guard_found: require_admin() at admin.py:9-11 aborts with 403 for non-admins, but ban() wraps it in try/except Exception (admin.py:16-19). The exception is swallowed and only logged, with no re-raise or return. There are no decorators or before_request hooks.
verdict_facts.reason: At admin.py:17-20 the 403 HTTPException raised by abort() at line 11 is caught by `except Exception` and only logged, so do_ban(uid) at line 20 runs for any authenticated non-admin; unban() at line 26 is unaffected because it calls require_admin outside a try block.
